answer.rationale: Memory_73 explicitly warns against generalizing promotional pricing as a growth strategy due to material 30-day retention damage—a critical risk when facing competitive price pressure, as retention collapse would compound churn. Memory_44 shows enterprise sales-assist works but this is a SMB-base emergency. Memory_86 and memory_91 both show reliable, durable activation and engagement lifts with positive or neutral retention impact. Activation_messaging (memory_91: +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention) directly addresses the root problem: getting at-risk SMB accounts to see product value faster, reducing price sensitivity. This buys time and reduces churn without sacrificing long-term unit economics or retention. A standard_experiment scale allows rapid deployment against the immediate churn spike while preserving ability to adjust. This strategy aligns with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue by defending retention and improving perceived value rather than discounting into a race to the bottom.
